Score-statistic meta-analysis

Source: vignettes/meta-analysis.Rmd
meta-analysis.Rmd

top_meta() combines score vectors and information matrices from any number of independent studies. This supports distributed analyses in which individual participant data cannot be pooled.

Required study-level objects

Each study supplies a list with:

  • score: a numeric score vector;
  • information: the corresponding square symmetric information matrix.

All studies must use the same parameter order and second-stage design.

library(TOP)

studies <- list(
  array_a = list(
    score = c(1.0, 2.0),
    information = diag(c(2, 3))
  ),
  array_b = list(
    score = c(0.5, -0.5),
    information = diag(c(1, 2))
  ),
  array_c = list(
    score = c(-0.25, 1.0),
    information = diag(c(4, 1))
  )
)

meta <- top_meta(studies)
meta
#> TOP score meta-analysis
#> Studies: 3 
#> Chi-squared: 1.2649 on 2 df; p = 0.5313
meta$score
#> [1] 1.25 2.50
meta$information
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    7    0
#> [2,]    0    6
meta$statistic
#> [1] 1.264881
meta$p.value
#> [1] 0.5312936

The combined score and information are sums across studies. TOP then evaluates the quadratic score statistic using the combined information matrix.

Defensive checks

top_meta() rejects non-finite scores, non-square or asymmetric information matrices, inconsistent parameter dimensions, and a singular combined information matrix. Align parameter names and allele coding before constructing the list; study-specific column mapping belongs in the analysis project rather than in the package.

ScoreMetaAnalysis() remains available for older two-study scripts, but new code should use top_meta().
